standard_text: Electric motors and generators: the motor effect and Fleming's left-hand rule; DC and AC generators and Faraday's law; alternating current: root mean square values, Vrms = Vmax/√2 and Pave = VrmsIrms; uses of AC and DC. (summary of the senior secondary Physics curriculum, SSS 3; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 Physics worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): motors, generators and transformers, motors and generators, peak and rms values, transformers and AC problems and magnetic fields and the motor principle. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A motor turns electrical energy into mechanical energy; a generator does the opposite.
body_html:
How to think about it

An electric motor works because a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a force (the motor effect); a split-ring commutator reverses the current every half turn so the coil keeps turning. A generator uses electromagnetic induction: a coil turning in a magnetic field has a changing flux, which induces an emf.

An AC generator uses slip rings and produces alternating current; a DC generator uses a split-ring commutator. The national grid in Nigeria supplies AC at 230 V (rms) and 50 Hz. The rms value is the DC value that would give the same power: Vrms = Vmax/√2, Irms = Imax/√2, and Pave = VrmsIrms.

Example

Vmax = 325 V. Vrms?

÷ √2

Answer: 230 V

Example

Which part of a DC motor reverses the current?

Two half rings

Answer: the split-ring commutator

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up slip rings and split rings.
  • Using peak values to find average power.
  • Thinking a generator makes energy from nothing.

faq.q: Why is electricity transmitted at very high voltage?
faq.a: For the same power the current is smaller, so less energy is lost as heat in the cables (P = I²R).

faq.q: Why is AC used for the grid?
faq.a: Its voltage can easily be stepped up and down with transformers.

items.q: A wire carries a current up the page in a magnetic field that points to the left. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the force on the wire?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field (to the left), seCond finger = Current (up the page), thuMb = Motion/force (out of the page).

items.q: You look at one end of a solenoid. The current flows anticlockwise around this end. What pole is this end?
